title: Jharkhand protest: Congress workers scuffle with police outside CEO office
text: Jharkhand protest: Congress workers scuffle with police outside CEO office. The youth wing and activists of Jharkhand Congress clashed with police on Tuesday while they were trying to cross the barricades during a protest happening outside the office of the chief electoral officer's (CEO) situated in Ranchi. These workers were protesting against the Election commission while demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, the chief election commissioner (CEC). According to the PTI report, some demonstrators blackened the commission's official nameplate after being stopped from entering the premises. The hundreds of congress and youth wing workers marched from the area near the old assembly building to the CEO's office in Dhurwa. They were carrying placards raised slogans, "Where will you find the vote thief? In the BJP office", "Gyanesh Kumar Resign" and "Vote thief, vacate your seat of power". Former Union minister Subodh Kant Sahay, who participated in the demonstration, alleged that people across the country had prepared a "chargesheet" against the CEC. "People of the country have prepared a chargesheet against the CEC. Allegations against the CEC are enough for a person holding a constitutional post to resign," Sahay said. The protest was aimed at highlighting the plight of people who, despite carrying the required documents, continue to make repeated trips to government offices to get their names added to the electoral rolls, a Congress leader said. "Democracy is being murdered... Two other members of the Election Commission had raised questions on Gyanesh Kumar's style of working, but now irregularities committed by him have come out," said Congress Ranchi Mahanagar president Kumar Raja. title: 'BJP winning in states it couldn't even at peak of Modi wave': Abhijeet Dipke says âno pointâ in polls
text: Dipke urged the CEC to resign, claiming that election results in the country had become "predetermined" and that participation in such polls had therefore become meaningless. PUNE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke alleged that the BJP is winning in states where it could not secure victories even during the peak of the "Modi wave", attributing the outcome to alleged institutional manipulation under chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "The BJP is winning in states where it couldn't even secure a victory during the peak of the 'Modi wave' and this is happening because of Gyanesh Kumar. Once Gyanesh Kumar leaves and the SIR freezes, only then will we know how many seats the BJP actually wins," Dipke told reporters on Sunday. Dipke urged the CEC to resign, claiming that election results in the country had become "predetermined" and that participation in such polls had therefore become meaningless. "I feel that until Gyanesh Kumar resigns and ensures free and fair elections, there is no point in participating in such polls, because the winner is already predetermined," he said. Dipke made the remarks during his visit to Pune to express solidarity with students protesting against the Maharashtra government over alleged irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations and recruitment backlogs. He linked the issue surrounding the polls to alleged administrative failures under the ruling dispensation and claimed that public trust in both competitive examinations and electoral processes had collapsed. Seeking the resignation of the MPSC Chairman, Dipke said, "I have come here to meet protesting students. Their future is in question because there are continuous cases of paper leaks. The government is not serious about these leaks. CJP supports their demands, and till MPSC chairman resigns, this protest will continue." text: Hyderabad : Escalating the Congress partyâs attack on the Election Commission over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Wednesday demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi ensure the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and scrap the exercise, warning that failure to do so would invite a larger political battle against the BJP-led govt. Speaking to reporters outside the Barakhamba Road police station in New Delhi, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was taken after being detained during a protest at Jantar Mantar, Revanth said the agitation against the CEC and the Centre would continue until Gyanesh Kumar stepped down or the SIR exercise was withdrawn. âThe detention of Rahul Gandhi and other AICC leaders has only exposed the intolerance of PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah . Instead of arresting those who have committed a mistake, the police, on the directions of Shah, took away Rahul Gandhi and other AICC leaders in their van on the lines of terrorists being forcibly arrested,â alleged Revanth. Revanth, accompanied by revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy, visited the police station to express solidarity with Gandhi and other opposition leaders. The chief minister said the Congress and the INDIA bloc would intensify their campaign under Rahul Gandhiâs leadership, taking the fight âfrom sadak to Sansadâ. âPM Modi and the BJP earlier misused ED, CBI and IT to win elections. Now, they are misusing the ECI to remove âanti-Modiâ and âanti-BJPâ voter names from the electoral rolls through SIR. The Constitution has guaranteed the voting right to its citizens, and no one has the right to snatch it. People are watching PM Modi and BJPâs game plan and will oust them from power because this is not the issue of the Congress but of the people of the country,â Revanth claimed. Revanth said the demand for the CECâs resignation was not merely a Congress issue but one concerning the voting rights of citizens. Reiterating the partyâs stand, he urged Modi and Shah to ensure Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation and said the Congress and INDIA bloc would continue their campaign to âsave the Constitutionâ and protect votersâ rights. title: No whataboutery can justify voter disenfranchisement, says SC judge; oppn says CEC 'exposed'
text: Justice Bhuyanâs remarks spark opposition attack on CEC NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process that "disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens" is âintrinsically arbitraryâ and a negation of the constitutional order. The remarks were then cited by opposition leaders to target Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. âIf any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,â Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying. He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14. âNo authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,â he said. On deletion of names from electoral rolls, Bhuyan said, âExcept in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing. From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body.â Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said Bhuyanâs remarks showed that the CEC had violated the Constitution âboth in letter and spiritâ. âJustice Bhuyan has said much more and has exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel. Gyanesh Kumar simply has lost all moral right to continue in office,â Ramesh said. text: The SC however refused to pass any interim direction in the matter NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP on Monday said the Supreme Court's decision to issue notices to the Election Commission (EC) and the Centre on pleas seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar showed that all institutions in the country were "functioning independently" and there was no atmosphere of "fear and dictatorship". "The country is moving in a very democratic way. Everyone is speaking their heart out. All procedures and systems are being followed. Where else could there be a better model of democracy? I feel India is celebrating democracy," BJP MP and spokesperson Sambit Patra told reporters at a news conference at the party headquarters in Delhi when asked about the development. Watch âWould See Who Modified Form 6â: Supreme Court Refuses To Suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar Also Read | SC seeks EC response on changes during SIR: Why has Form 6 become a flashpoint â explained Patra's remarks came after the Supreme Court sought responses from the EC and the Centre within a week on a plea challenging the manner in which the poll panel, led by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, allegedly took decisions without the approval of the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. However, a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to pass any interim order in the matter. The bench observed that it could not pass an order merely on the basis of a media report, which may or may not be accurate. However, it asserted that if any decisions of the EC were found to have been taken unilaterally by the CEC, the Supreme Court could reconsider or recall them. "They (EC) are expected to take unanimous decisions. If there is no unanimity, it has to be by majority. If records show some decision was not unanimous, etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra vires. Can we ex parte come to a decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," the CJI said. The controversy stems from an Indian Express report published late last month, which claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The report alleged that some of these decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. Also Read | 'Form 6 has not been approved by us': What SC said on EC's SIR decision - top quotes According to the report, the poll panel's ECINet software added a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR in Form 6, the voter registration form, without the legal amendment required under election rules. The two commissioners reportedly objected to the change. The EC has since restored Form 6 to its original format in states where the SIR has been completed. However, the requirement continues in states and Union territories where the roll revision is still underway. Responding to the Indian Express report, the commission said that "differing views and observations" among its members were a "normal part" of deliberations in any multi-member institution. The EC also stated that all decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously by Kumar and the two Election Commissioners. Rahul Gandhi ups the ante against CEC Meanwhile, Congress MP and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi upped the ante against Kumar after the Supreme Court clarified that it did not approve any modification made by the EC in Form 6. In a social media post on X, the Congress leader accused the CEC of changing the application citizens use to register as new electors "illegally and unilaterally." title: Delhi Police yet to clear October 2 Jantar Mantar protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: Delhi Police has not granted permission for the planned protest at Jantar Mantar (In frame, from L to R: adv Prashant Bhushan, RJD MP Manoj Jha, Neha Bora) NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has so far not granted permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 2 against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, police sources said. The proposed demonstration has been called by social activists and student groups over issues related to the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, news agency ANI reported. According to police sources, permission has not been granted for the proposed gathering at Jantar Mantar so far. The protest is scheduled to be held on Gandhi Jayanti, with organisers calling for action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Delhi Police has also put up barricades on roads leading to the Jantar Mantar area amid the proposed protest call. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj had on Monday made a public call for people to join the Jantar Mantar protest. title: Vijay's TVK joins INDIA bloc meet in Tamil Nadu, Congress calls it 'historic day'
text: Congress is in alliance with Vijay's TVK in Tamil Nadu. NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore on Saturday described the participation of actor-politician Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the INDIA bloc's Tamil Nadu meeting as a "historic day", saying the party's entry would strengthen the opposition alliance in the state. An INDIA bloc meeting was held at the TNCC office in Chennai under Tagore's leadership, with Congress, TVK, CPM, CPI, VCK, MDMK and IUML participating. The meeting focused on the opposition's demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and its broader campaign over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. According to ANI, TVK was represented at the meeting by party leaders Aadhav Arjuna and Maria Wilson. Watch INDIA Bloc Meet: Rahul Gandhil, Mamata, Kharge Target CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over SIR-EC Row Addressing reporters after the meeting, Tagore said Vijay-led TVK had joined the INDIA bloc and said its entry would strengthen the bloc in Tamil Nadu. "Vijay-led TVK has joined the INDIA alliance. It's a very historic day for the INDIA alliance. The INDIA alliance, particularly in Tamil Nadu, is to be strengthened by the entry of TVK," Tagore said, according to ANI. Tagore also linked the development to the opposition's political contest with the BJP, saying the fight against the BJP and the policies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah would become "interesting" in Tamil Nadu. The meeting also decided to intensify protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Tagore said INDIA bloc parties would hold demonstrations at district headquarters across Tamil Nadu, followed by a joint protest in Chennai on October 15. "We have decided to have the district-level demonstrations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. We demand his resignation," Tagore said, adding that the participating parties would release the list of leaders taking part in the demonstrations. He said all seven parties participating in Saturday's meeting would join the Chennai protest on October 15. MDMK general secretary Vaiko said the meeting had welcomed TVK's participation and appreciated the presence of its leader, Vijay. He also announced a series of statewide rallies against the Chief Election Commissioner on October 13, 14 and 15, according to ANI. title: Declare SIR and related decisions void: Plea in SC
text: Fresh SC plea seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumarâs suspension over unilateral powers NEW DELHI: A fresh petition filed in SC in the ongoing row surrounding CEC Gyanesh Kumar has sought his suspension and declaration that CEC cannot take unilateral decisions on EC's behalf. It also sought that Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and all actions, decisions, directions and consequential measures undertaken pursuant to the exercise be declared void ab initio (invalid) and without lawful authority. Referring to media reports, petitioner Rakesh Singh alleged about 14 decisions were taken in the name of EC despite objections recorded by the two other ECs - Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. He sought a direction to CEC to "show under what authority he has acted, and continues to act" as though he is individually entitled to exercise collective decision-making power vested by Article 324 of Constitution in EC. "Issue a writ in the nature of quo warranto (by what authority), or other appropriate writ, order or direction, calling upon Respondent No. 3 Gyanesh Kumar to show under what authority he has acted, and continues to act, as though entitled individually to exercise collective decision-making power vested by Art 324 in EC as a body," plea said. title: SIR row: Will annul Election Commission orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
text: âDecisions must be unanimous or by majorityâ, says Supreme Court NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday asked the Election Commission , CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to clarify whether crucial decisions regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls were taken unilaterally by the CEC, and said it would injunct (bar) those decisions by the three-member commission which were neither unanimous nor by majority. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said irrespective of powers vested in the CEC, the law clearly mandates that all decisions must either be by unanimity or by majority among the three members of the EC. âIf we come across instances (where CEC has unilaterally taken decisions), we will annul them,â it said. Watch âWould See Who Modified Form 6â: Supreme Court Refuses To Suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar The statement came after senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, strongly argued for an interim direction to the EC to only take decisions by unanimity during pendency of the petition as the amended CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, gave the CEC enormous powers. The PIL has sought scrutiny of the validity of SIR decisions and âalterationsâ in Form 6 for new voters. Singh said since the court could not undo elections, a direction must be issued that in the interregnum, EC must follow the statutory mandate. He pleaded that EC be directed to preserve all records on SIR decisions and Form 6 alteration and produce them before SC for scrutiny. CEC, ECs need to either rebut or endorse allegations about âunilateral decisionsâ Let us have some authenticated facts before us through their responses. They must respond in a clear and transparent manner. If the records show some of the decisions are not taken by majority, we will injunct those. But we cannot put the cart before the horse, the bench said while also issuing notices to the Centre, deputy EC Manish Garg and ECâs director general (IT) Seema Khanna. This has set the stage for the CEC and, more crucially, the two ECs to either endorse or rebut the allegation that important decisions on SIR were taken by Gyanesh Kumar unilaterally and in violation of the law which lays down that the commissionâs calls are to be made either unanimously or, failing that, by majority. The allegation, based on a newspaper report, is at the core of the controversy which has reignited opposition to SIR. Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for a PIL petitioner, also questioned the validity of Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provided that âno court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is, or was, a CEC or an election commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or functionâ. He said this was way beyond the immunity enjoyed even by SC judges and especially when it was not extended even to the PM. Justice Bagchi said, âWe will examine the expression âor wasâ. Protection while in office is understandable. Such protection (as provided under Section 16) is perhaps only with regard to the President. It is not given to constitutional court judges under Judges Inquiry Act.â Singh pleaded for suspension of the CEC or divesting him of his authority. When the bench asked who would conduct elections, Singh said the other two ECs would do it. He said in the interim, the SC-mandated selection panel for CEC should be brought back in which the CJI is included along with the PM and the LoP. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union minister nominated by the PM. title: âThey have become Ghajinisâ: Fadnavis mocks Uddhav, Raj Thackeray over Mumbai protest against EC
text: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis criticized Uddhav Thackeray and Raj Thackeray for their recent protest against the Election Commission. MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday hit out at Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and MNS chief Raj Thackeray over their joint protest march in Mumbai, calling the cousins âGhajinisâ and accusing them of venting frustration against the Election Commission after being rejected by voters. Fadnavis said the rally, held to demand the ouster of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and reforms in the electoral process, was an attempt by the Thackerays to regain lost political ground. âDespite all the hype, the attendance at the march was thin,â Fadnavis told reporters in Nagpur on the sidelines of a programme. Taking a dig at the cousins, he referred to the 2008 Hindi film Ghajini, whose protagonist suffers from short-term memory loss. âThey have become like âGhajiniâ. I want to remind these âGhajinisâ that Gyanesh Kumar became Chief Election Commissioner in 2025, whereas elections in Maharashtra were held in 2024, and SIR began in 2026,â Fadnavis said. âHow can the SIR of 2026 and the person who became Chief Election Commissioner in 2025 affect the 2024 elections?â he asked. Fadnavis also accused the opposition leaders of making false claims about the electoral process. âOne should at least try to sound believable while speaking lies. But they are blatantly speaking falsehoods, and when people have rejected them, they vent their frustration here on the Election Commission,â he said. Earlier on Sunday, Uddhav and Raj Thackeray jointly led the âGarjanaâ protest march from Metro Cinema to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters in south Mumbai. The rally focused on demands including scrapping Special Intensive Revisions (SIR) of electoral rolls, restoring paper ballots and changing the system for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner. The organisers also demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar. The protest was held without party flags, with only the national tricolour allowed. Congress leaders Balasaheb Thorat and Vijay Wadettiwar, along with NCP (SP) leaders Jayant Patil, Shashikant Shinde, Jitendra Awhad and Anil Deshmukh, participated in the rally. The crowd was estimated at around 8,000-10,000 and stretched from the Metro Cinema junction towards the BMC headquarters. Uddhav attacks EC, questions SIR Addressing the gathering, Uddhav accused Gyanesh Kumar of functioning as a âweaponâ for the BJP and demanded greater accountability in the electoral system. He questioned the Centre's stated objective behind SIR and asked how many illegal Bangladeshi immigrants had actually been identified and removed from electoral rolls through the exercise. âIf SIRs were conducted to weed out Bangladeshis from the votersâ list, then how many of them residing illegally in the country did the government find?â Uddhav asked. He also questioned how large numbers of illegal immigrants could have entered Maharashtra when the international border is controlled by the Centre. Uddhav claimed that around 13 crore voters had been deleted from draft electoral rolls across the country, describing the figure as roughly equivalent to Maharashtra's population. Citing the restoration of some deleted voters in West Bengal, he said re-verifying all voters left out nationwide could take about 144 months. He also demanded reforms in the appointment of the CEC, questioning why the post itself could not be decided through an election. âIf we can have elections for the President, why can't we have an election for the CEC who is responsible for conducting elections across the entire country?â Uddhav said. He criticised the present selection mechanism, pointing out that the Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union minister on the selection panel. Uddhav also questioned the legal protection available to the CEC and asked why the poll chief enjoyed protection from prosecution for actions taken while holding the post. Raj Thackeray raises Maharashtra vote figures Raj Thackeray questioned the increase in the number of voters in Maharashtra between the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections. He claimed that nearly one crore votes were added during the six-month period between the two elections. Raj said the BJP's vote count increased from around 2.4 crore in the Lok Sabha polls to 3.1 crore in the assembly election. He argued that such changes could undermine public confidence in the electoral process. NCP (SP) state president Shashikant Shinde also questioned the status of nearly two crore voters who, he alleged, had been declared bogus but were still able to vote in the assembly election. Congress leader Balasaheb Thorat alleged that the MVA's defeat in Maharashtra was the result of âvote theftâ and said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had repeatedly raised the issue and presented evidence. Police book rally organisers The rally later led to a police case against its organisers for allegedly holding the protest without permission. Azad Maidan police invoked Sections 223, 189 and 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to disobedience of an order by a public servant and offences linked to unlawful assembly. Uddhav also used the rally to highlight Maharashtra's drought situation, citing the plight of farmers and referring to a farmer family in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar whose soybean, chilli and corn crops allegedly failed, leaving the family burdened with loans. He said the farmer's son later died by suicide. The protest came two days after another demonstration in Mumbai demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. title: Scrap SIR, remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar: Prakash Raj
text: Thiruvananthapuram: Actor Prakash Raj on Wednesday demanded that Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be scrapped and chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar removed. He also called for the repeal of the immunity granted to CEC, reversal of changes to the appointment process and restoration of Chief Justice of India on the selection panel. Addressing a press meet in the city, Raj alleged that the SIR exercise is being used to delete votersâ names and weaken democracy and said that civil society should protest to save the country. He questioned the decision to introduce SIR within six months of Election Commission updating the electoral rolls. Raj alleged that the exercise is aimed at dividing the country and removing adivasis, dalits, minorities, Muslims, Christians and people with left-leaning views from the electoral rolls. He also said that the court did not stop SIR in Bihar and West Bengal but has now sent notices to Election Commission. He also asked who had decided to introduce SIR and alleged that there had been no response to Right to Information queries seeking details of when and how the decision was taken. âThere is no minutes of the meeting that discussed the need for SIR,â he added. âThey cannot kill people, so they kill citizenship,â he said. He urged citizens to come out in protest, alleging that political parties treated voters as âmachinesâ and that the exercise is taking away peopleâs right to choose their representatives and they are deciding who should vote. In Karnataka , Raj said civil society groups had pointed out that the state had around 5.5 crore voters and that the revision could not be completed in a month. He said they had sought six months to complete the exercise, but the demand was not accepted. He alleged that one crore voters had been classified under the ASDDO (absent, shifted, dead, duplicate and other) category. âI visited 23 districts in Karnataka. Seven lakh attempts had been made to delete votersâ names in the state. In some cases, one person had filed 200 to 500 applications seeking deletion of names,â he said. He said that people are being removed from the votersâ list for flimsy reasons, such as not being present at the house when the election staff visited. âOne man was out on a walk and his name got deleted. They tell him to apply again. People are worried that they will lose govt benefits they get because their names are no longer on the voterâs list,â Raj added. âIf this is the number in Karnataka, what about the other states?â he asked. He criticised the use of Form 6, saying people who had shifted residence could not be asked to apply as new voters and declare that they had never voted before. He also alleged that questions related to Citizenship Amendment Act were being asked in Form 16. Raj also said that the language of the warning given in the forms about a wrong declaration is not suitable for a democracy. He claimed that the process is disadvantaging people who are not familiar with technology. He further alleged that attempts could be made to use artificial intelligence to map votersâ political preferences and delete names accordingly. title: From climbing barricades to Akashvani Bhawan twist: High drama at Rahul-led CEC protest - how it unfolded
text: From Parliament to Akashvani Bhawan - Rahul climbs barricades, MPs detained NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi climbed atop barricades during the INDIA bloc MPsâ march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters in New Delhi on Tuesday, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation over irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule and several other opposition leaders also joined the march, which was held amid heavy security and barricading around Parliament and the EC office. Security personnel stopped the march near the NITI Aayog office as the MPs raised slogans of âVote Chor, Gaddi Chhodâ. Watch Rahul Climbs Barricade, Enters Akashvani Bhawan With Priyanka During EC March Against Gyanesh Kumar INDIA bloc MPs stopped near Niti Aayog Rahul Gandhi led several INDIA bloc MPs in a march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters in New Delhi, with protesters carrying placards and cutouts of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The opposition MPs were demanding Kumarâs removal over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. The INDIA bloc had announced the march from Parliament to Nirvachan Sadan as part of its campaign against the Election Commissionâs handling of the electoral roll revision. The protest route saw heavy security deployment, with barricades placed across central Delhi and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the march. Security personnel stopped the MPs near NITI Aayog, preventing them from proceeding towards the ECI headquarters. Several opposition MPs then sat in protest near Parliament Street. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) skipped the march, saying it would pursue the issue through its own means. Opposition leaders detained Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc MPs tried to enter the Election Commission office during their protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, but were stopped by security personnel. After being prevented from entering the EC office complex, Congress leaders staged a sit-in outside the premises. The INDIA bloc MPs had marched from Parliament towards Nirvachan Sadan, demanding Kumarâs resignation. Earlier, Rahul Gandhi climbed atop heavy iron barriers near the NITI Aayog office and waved the tricolour while advancing towards the EC headquarters. Tensions escalated as Delhi Police detained Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, party General Secretary KC Venugopal and several other INDIA bloc leaders near the NITI Aayog office, where police had barricaded the route to prevent the opposition MPs from reaching Nirvachan Sadan. Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi enter Akashvani Bhawan premises during EC protest Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with some other supporters, entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises in an attempt to reach the Election Commission office during the INDIA blocâs protest demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation. The Congress leaders and other MPs were earlier stopped by security personnel on Parliament Street near the NITI Aayog office while marching towards the EC headquarters. After being prevented from proceeding further, they sat on the road in protest. Rahul Gandhi and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee later climbed atop a police barricade, while Priyanka Gandhi was taken to a waiting bus for detention. Priyanka Gandhi soon alighted from the bus and joined Rahul Gandhi at the Akashvani gate. Despite being stopped by police, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and Congress MP Deepender Hooda entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises through the reception gate and were later seen sitting under a tree. Security tightened around protest route The march began amid heavy security deployment and barricading in and around Parliament and the Election Commission headquarters. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut questioned the security arrangements, saying the MPs intended to proceed peacefully. He also alleged that the CEC had âno moral rightâ to continue in office, while CPI leader P Sandosh Kumar called him a âCheating Election Commissionerâ. Kharge, Akhilesh target EC over SIR as INDIA bloc MPs press for poll reforms Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the Modi government was trying to take away the publicâs right to vote and accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting at the governmentâs direction. âAfter independence, the public was given the right to vote, which the Modi government is trying to end. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is the government's puppet. Gyanesh Kumar does exactly what Modi and Shah say. This will end democracy and the Constitution, and establish dictatorship. The INDIA alliance is fighting against this injustice. We will continue to fight and we will win,â Kharge said. On the INDIA bloc MPsâ protest march, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Arvind Sawant said, âWe want Gyanesh Kumar to be removed, elections to be held on ballot papers, and thirdly, all the people whose names were struck off in the SIR here should be reinstated.â Sawant also alleged, âThe Bharatiya Janata Party has a direct connection with the Election Commission.â Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav also raised the issue, according to the statement shared from Delhi. Opposition steps up attack over SIR The protest is part of the oppositionâs sustained campaign against the SIR exercise and its demand for greater transparency from the poll panel. Congress MP Dharamveer Gandhi alleged that 13 crore votes had been deleted and called it the âbiggest fraud in Indian political historyâ. Congress MP Imran Masood accused Kumar of eroding public trust in the Election Commission, while CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the Supreme Courtâs observations had strengthened the oppositionâs objections to the additional declaration attached to Form 6. âThe main demands are crystal clear. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar must go; he should resign. The SIR (Special Intensive Revision) should be scrapped. All the voters who have been removed or deleted under SIR must be restored back onto the voter list,â Congress Rajya Sabha MP Syed Naseer Hussain told ANI. He also demanded a high-level inquiry into alleged political interference in the election machinery. Form 6 row fuels political clash The march comes a day after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modified version of Form 6 and said it would examine the Election Commissionâs records to determine whether changes had been made and who had authorised them. The EC had earlier said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court and that the forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, would be used outside the SIR period. Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram said, âHow can the BJP blatantly deny that the Chief Justice of India did not say that... he said it clearly, 'we have not approved any modifications to Form 6.' I have seen the declaration... title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar must resign to protect ECâs credibility: TPCC chief
text: TPCC chief Mahesh Kumar Goud, minister D Sridhar Babu and others at the protest in Hyderabad on Monday. Pic: Venkat Rao M Hyderabad: Congress ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs along with party workers staged protest demonstrations in all the district headquarters and a main rally was organised in Hyderabad under the leadership of Telangana Congress president B Mahesh Kumar Goud on Monday, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to protect the independence, credibility and institutional integrity of the Election Commission of India . Mahesh Goud told reporters that Election Commissionâs conduct was undermining democracy in the country and claimed that elections were being manipulated. âThe actions of the poll panel are detrimental to democracy and the future of voters is at stake. The CEC of India has become a stooge of the BJP. The electoral process is being influenced to benefit the ruling BJP at the Centre,â he alleged. Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka said the repeated warnings given by AICC senior leader Rahul Gandhi that citizensâ voting rights were being systematically undermined through âvote theftâ in the country over the past few years have now been proved true. He expressed deep concern over the manner in which citizensâ votes were allegedly being deleted in the name of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, stating that the acknowledgement of the issue by election commissioners themselves was an unfortunate development for the countryâs democracy. âRahul Gandhi had been fighting from the beginning to protect the Constitution and the voting rights of citizens. All political parties that believe in democracy and the Constitution should set aside their differences and join hands with the Congress in the fight to protect democratic values. Only those who do not have faith in the Constitution are staying away from the movement,â claimed Bhatti. In the memorandum, the PCC chief expressed serious concern over the functioning of ECI, its decision-making process and the issues emerging in connection with the SIR process during the tenure of Gyanesh Kumar as CEC of India. Leaders also stated that reports indicating that more than 13 crore names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls in 30 states and union territories as part of the SIR process were a matter of serious concern. Although Election Commission has stated that these were deletions from the draft electoral rolls and that statutory procedures were available for filing claims, objections and restoration of names, Congress party made it clear that the reports of deletions on such a massive scale required the highest levels of transparency, accountability and independent scrutiny. Major demands of Congress Gyanesh Kumar must resign from the post of CEC of India, taking responsibility for questions concerning the functioning of Election Commission and public confidence in it. The minutes of meetings, orders, notes, objections and related records concerning the decisions reportedly questioned by the two election commissioners should be placed in the public domain to the extent legally permissible. An independent, transparent and comprehensive review should be conducted into reports that more than 13 crore names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls during the SIR process. The review should also examine whether any eligible voters were inadvertently deleted. Election Commission should disclose complete state-wise and constituency-wise details of the names deleted under the SIR, the reasons for deletion and the number of names restored after claims and objections. Election Commission should provide a clear public explanation regarding the objections reportedly recorded by the two election commissioners and disclose how those objections were considered before final decisions were taken. Strong safeguards must be put in place to ensure that no eligible citizen loses the right to vote due to administrative errors, inadequate verification, failure to receive proper notice or procedural lapses. text: A protest occurred at Jantar Mantar where activists opposed alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls (Photo credit: X) NEW DELHI: A woman at Jantar Mantar on Friday was seen attempting to stop a police vehicle carrying detained protesters during the protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in a moment that drew comparisons with Rhiya Ahirâs viral protest visual from Mumbai. title: 'Want to see who modified Form 6': SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: SC on Monday heard two pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC and the other two election commissioners on a plea challenging decisions taken by the poll body on Special Intensive Revision. A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether Gyanesh used powers belonging to the Election Commission without the approval of election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. âAny modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,â the CJI noted. The apex court directed the respondents to file their responses to the allegations. The court said it would examine whether the statutory scheme was followed and indicated that if the records showed that any decision was not taken in accordance with the law, it could injunct such a decision and hold it ultra vires. "If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires. Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added. What did the petitioners seek? One of the plea sought Gyanesh's suspension until the final hearing to protect the âmulti-member character of the Election Commissionâ. It asked that Sandhu and Joshi run the commission's business together in the meantime and that any vacancy be filled on the recommendation of a committee that includes the Chief Justice of India. However, the second plea sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials for allegedly failing in their official duty. It further sought a declaration that all decisions, guidelines and software changes made under Gyanesh without the full commission's agreement are âunconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initioâ, meaning illegal and invalid from the start. Tripathi's plea relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which says the majority view prevails when commissioners differ. The plea argued that the law requires decisions to be taken together. What is the EC SIR row? A report by the Indian Express claimed that commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders relating to the SIR, which were allegedly issued without their knowledge or recommendation. text: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh; CEC Gyanesh Kumar NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused the Election Commission (EC) of âlyingâ about its ECINet portal, alleging that the platform was not in accordance with the law. Congress MP Jairam Ramesh also questioned the "intentions" of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, describing them as ânot honest.â âIn its damage-control but actually damage-enhancing press note on September 26, 2026, the Election Commission of India had promised a committee to certify that the legally suspect ECINet âcomplies with the provisions of the Acts and Rulesâ. In reality, this should never have been in doubt at all in the first place if the intentions of the CEC Gyanesh Kumar were honestâwhich they were not,â Ramesh wrote on X. He was referring to the poll panelâs statement last week, issued days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which they maintained had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation. âECINet was launched on January 22, 2026, with much fanfare to âenhance transparency, credibility and public trustâ. The ECI press note issued that day assured the country that it âhas been developed in strict accordance with the lawâ and in full compliance with the Constitution of India, the Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960,â Ramesh wrote. âAll of this was a lie,â he added. Ramesh further accused the EC of "violating" laws governing the electoral process. âBy restricting Electoral Registration Officersâ (EROs) access to the ECINet voter-roll system and overruling EROs in states such as Goa and West Bengal, among others, the ECI under the CEC has violated the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. Both laws establish that EROs have statutory authority over electoral rolls,â he posted. title: Raj Thackeray by side, Uddhav Thackeray asks: Why is CEC more protected than PM Modi?
text: Demanding reforms in the process of appointment of the poll chief, Uddhav questioned why the post is not subject to a vote. MUMBAI: The scrapping of special intensive revisions (SIRs) of electoral rolls, a return to paper ballots, and elections for the post of the chief election commissioner (CEC) formed the core demands at the joint âGarjanaâ protest rally organised by Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray and MNS chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday. Uddhav accused Kumar of acting as a âweaponâ for BJP. He warned âBJP and these officialsâ of prosecution on the lines of the Nuremberg trials conducted for leaders of Nazi Germany. â[They] should realise that a similar thing will happen in the country.â Watch âDhappaâ: Rahul Gandhi Dodges Police, Pulls Off Akashvani Bhawan Surprise With Priyanka Addressing a crowd of 8,000-10,000 that stretched from the Metro Cinema junction to the BMC headquarters in south Mumbai, the cousins called for structural changes to the electoral process. The demonstration was organised without any party flags; only the tricolour was allowed. Many netas from other MVA parties participated as well. Azad Maidan police later registered a case against the organisers for holding the rally without permission. The protest came two days after CJPâs stir in the city seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumarâs ouster. Uddhav sought data on the number of illegal Bangladeshis detected since SIRs began. âIf SIRs were conducted to weed out Bangladeshis from the votersâ list, then how many of them residing illegally in the country did govt find?â He asked how so many illegal Bangladeshis as alleged reached Maharashtra in the first place when the border is controlled by the Centre. He alleged that 13 crore voters stand deleted nationwide from draft electoral rollsââroughly equivalent to the entire population of Maharashtraâ. Citing the case of West Bengal, where some deleted voters were restored to the rolls, Uddhav noted that re-checking all voters who have been left out nationwide would take âapproximately 144 monthsâ. Raj questioned the addition of nearly 1 crore votes for BJP in Maharashtra in the six months between the Lok Sabha elections and the assembly polls in 2024. âIn those six months, 40-60 lakh votes were added to the rolls. BJP got 2.4 crore votes in the Lok Sabha elections and 3.1 crore in the assembly elections,â he said. He said fear of loss of peopleâs faith in themâthereby resulting in loss of votesâusually deters those in govt from engaging in such poll roll manipulations. âBut this fear is non-existent in the state and Union govts,â he said. State NCP (SP) president Shashikanth Shinde asked what poll officials and state govt plan to do about the â2 crore voters declared bogusâ who cast their votes in the assembly elections. Congressâs Balasaheb Thorat asserted that MVAâs loss in Maharashtra âwas made possible only through the stealing of votesâ. He said Rahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, has been flagging âvote theftâ for a long time and had also presented evidence of it. âAll those who gained power did so through the theft of votes. They used various methods. Gyanesh Kumar is a symbol of this corrupt administration,â he alleged. âThe period since 2014 (of NDAâs governance) will be remembered as a âdark periodâ in the countryâs history.â Demanding reforms in the process of appointment of the poll chief, Uddhav questioned why the post is not subject to a vote. âIf we can have elections for the President, why canât we have an election for the CEC who is responsible for conducting elections across the entire country?â Uddhav also criticised changes to the CEC selection panel. âThe selection committee earlier used to comprise the PM, the CJI and the leader of the opposition, but now, they have replaced the CJI with a minister of govtâs choice. â He questioned the legal protection granted to the CEC. âBy law, the CEC cannot be hauled up and prosecuted for his time as the commissioner. Why does the CEC have such protection that even the PM doesnât have?â Uddhav also spoke about the drought conditions in the state. âToday, Maharashtra is facing a famine. We canât even imagine the condition of the famine-plagued farmer today.â Citing the case of one such farmer, Jijabai Kachate, he said she planted soybean in her field in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, which failed. âShe then planted chillies, which too failed. Later, she planted corn, which also failed. The loans piled up. The banks came calling. And then her son died by suicide in the same field. The same field where she saw her future, she saw her sonâs final rites,â he said. While Rajâs son, Amit, attended the rally, Uddhavâs son, Aaditya, was unwell and could not attend it, said Shiv Sena (UBT) functionaries. Police invoked Sections 223 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by a public servant), 189 (unlawful assembly) and 190 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object) of BNS in the case filed against the protestâs organisers. title: Second full EC meet in 5 days, SIR extended again in Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya
text: Chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar with election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi NEW DELHI: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days, and decided to extend the deadlines for the ongoing SIR exercise in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya, reports Bharti Jain. The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16. For Meghalaya, the date for publication of the final poll roll has been revised to Oct 26. The second full meeting of the commission since an Indian Express report alleged that ECs Sandhu and Joshi had objected to steps taken by EC on 14 occasions over 10 months reaffirms that the CEC and the two ECs have agreed to sit together and transact normal business of the commission through regular meetings. The draft roll of Meghalaya published on Aug 5 listed 21.7 lakh electors, with around 7.7% absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors deleted. title: An open door is more powerful than a closed argument, Kamal Haasan tells CEC
text: Kamal Haasan CHENNAI: Rajya Sabha member and Makkal Needhi Maiam (MNM) founder Kamal Haasan has appealed to chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to initiate urgent steps to restore public trust in the Election Commission of India (ECI) and urged him to meet Opposition Members of Parliament at the Samvidhan Bhavan in the Parliament complex. He sent an open letter to the CEC in this regard on Wednesday. The letter comes in the backdrop of heightened tensions following the detention of opposition leaders in New Delhi as they attempted to meet the Election Commissioners to raise grievances regarding electoral integrity and voter roll revisions. Highlighting that the credibility of the Indian Republic depends entirely on the credibility of its elections, Kamal outlined several core issues fuelling public apprehension over electoral processes. Expressing concern over the "rushed and erroneous implementation" of SIR, Kamal warned that stringent documentation requirements risk disenfranchising eligible voters, particularly those from socio-economically weaker sections. The letter pointed to growing worries regarding recent alterations to Form 6 (voter registration), allegations of selective enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), and the unabated flow of unaccounted money in political campaigns. The MP raised concerns over the alleged deployment of central investigative agencies in contexts that trigger political defections and undermine the independence of elected representatives. Critiquing the detention of opposition leaders who sought an audience with the Commission, Kamal stated that such measures cannot be the way forward when institutional trust is being tested. "This is not a request on behalf of one political party. It is an appeal in the larger national interest," he wrote, inviting the CEC and fellow commissioners to meet Opposition MPs at Samvidhan Bhavan. Concluding the letter, the actor-turned-politician emphasised that maintaining public faith requires visible impartiality, noting, "At a time when trust in democratic institutions must be strengthened, an open door can be more powerful than a closed argument." text: 'PM Modi uses Gyanesh Kumar to steal elections': Rahul Gandhi on SIR irregularities NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday questioned the legal immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi uses him to âsteal electionsâ. In a post on X, Gandhi wrote, âQ. Why is CEC Gyanesh Kumar the only Indian with lifelong blanket legal immunity? A. Because PM Modi uses him to steal elections.â This comes as top leaders of the INDIA bloc met in New Delhi on Wednesday to finalise an action plan for a joint agitation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the Congress asserting that the opposition stands united to protect the Constitution from "repeated assaults" by the Modi government, including its alleged "vote chori gameplan" to remain in power. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chiefs Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, AICC general secretaries Jairam Ramesh and K C Venugopal, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, and leaders of the SP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP(SP) and Shiv Sena (UBT), among others, attended the meeting. "The INDIA janbandhan meeting just got underway. The parties participating are the Congress, Samajwadi Party, All India Trinamool Congress, NCP(SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), Rashtriya Janata Dal, CPI(M), CPI, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, CPI-ML, IUML, Kerala Congress (M), Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, RevolutionarySocialist Party, Kerala Congress (Jacob) and All India Forward Bloc," Ramesh said in a post on X. "These and other Opposition parties stand united to protect the Constitution of India from repeated assaults of the Modi Government - most recently its Vote Chori gameplan through the ECI to remain in power," he added. Sources said a draft notice for a fresh motion seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was ready and would be discussed at the meeting for approval. The DMK and AAP did not attend the meeting, while SP chief Akhilesh Yadav was also absent due to the Rajya Sabha nomination process in Uttar Pradesh. The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying they had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation. text: A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park. title: Oct 2 anti-CEC protests: Jantar Mantar in Delhi, Shivaji Park in Mumbai; all you need to know about the planned stir
text: Organisers have announced separate gatherings, while police clearance remains pending at both proposed locations. NEW DELHI: Protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar have been announced in Delhi and Mumbai and other cities for October 2, with parties demanding his resignation and raising issues concerning the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Hereâs what is planned and where the permission situation stands: Delhi | October 2: A proposed protest against Gyanesh Kumar is scheduled at Jantar Mantar on Gandhi Jayanti. However, Delhi Police have not granted permission as of October 1, according news agency PTI. Barricades have also been placed on roads leading to the protest area. Who is backing the Delhi protest: Social activists and student groups have called the demonstration, while opposition groups are also expected to participate or hold parallel protests. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj had appealed to people to join the Jantar Mantar protest. Mumbai | October 2: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, has announced a âJail Bharo Andolanâ against Kumar at Shivaji Park at 4pm, Gate No. 6. Mumbai permission status: Mumbai Police have not granted permission for the proposed Shivaji Park gathering. Police said they were not empowered to approve such a gathering there in view of a 2013 Bombay High Court order and described the area as a silence zone. Organisers were advised to seek an alternative venue. CJPâs stated position: Dipke has said the protests will continue until Gyanesh Kumar resigns and has announced plans for demonstrations in Goa, Karnataka, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand. He has also warned of a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi later in October if Kumar does not step down. Its announced programme includes district-level marches from October 2-8, a march to the ECI headquarters on October 6, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and a mega rally in Delhi on November 1. The protests come amid a wider political dispute over the Election Commissionâs functioning and the SIR exercise. The Election Commission has defended its procedures, while opposition parties and protest organisers have raised allegations and demands for changes. text: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke addresses a press conference as Co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka look on. NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Thursday demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar within 48 hours, accusing him of undermining votersâ rights and warning of a nationwide protest if he does not step down. Speaking at a press conference, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that the electoral process had been âriggedâ and that citizensâ right to vote was being taken away. Watch âAnti-Nationalâ Gyanesh Kumar Must Resign: CJPâs Dipke, Saurav Das List 3 Demands Amid SIR-EC Row The three demands The 1st demand: Gyanesh Kumar must resign within 48 hours. Initiate criminal proceedings against him. Answer who gave him the orders to steal votes. The 2nd demand: Immediately halt all upcoming elections, freeze the SIR, and restore the January 2025 voter list. The 3rd demand: Repeal the 2023 law on the appointment of Election Commissioners and enact a new law that inspires public confidence, built with active participation from civil society. â Jantar Mantar 2.0 will definitely happenâ Dipke warned that the party would begin protests across the country if Kumar did not resign within the 48-hour deadline. âIf Gyanesh Kumar does not resign within 48 hours, we will start a nationwide protest, before coming for a protest in Delhi,â Dipke said, adding that if the CEC doesn't resign, âJantar Mantar 2.0 will definitely happenâ. He also said opposition parties should reconsider participating in elections if they believed the electoral process was being rigged. âIf you know elections are being rigged, you cannot participate. You will have to take a stand,â he said. Dipke alleged that Kumar was the âbiggest threat to Indian democracyâ and accused the Election Commission of deciding who would be allowed to vote. âWho is Gyanesh to revoke our right to vote?â he said, calling for criminal proceedings against the CEC. CJP cited exclusions of more than two crore names each in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, around one crore in Karnataka, 97 lakh in Tamil Nadu, 90 lakh in West Bengal, 73 lakh in Telangana, 47 lakh in Delhi and 24 lakh in Kerala. âDemocracy means people choose their govt. This is not democracy, this is autocracy. Under Gyanesh Kumar, we are seeing an electoral system in which Election Commission is deciding who remains on the voter rolls and who does not,â Dipke said. Questions over SIR within Election Commission The remarks came a day after The Indian Express reported that questions had repeatedly been raised within the three-member Election Commission over issues related to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. According to the report, election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR. The report said the objections included four instances on a single day and involved decisions that Sandhu and Joshi said were taken or issued without their knowledge. The nationwide rollout of the SIR has been under the supervision of all three election commissioners. title: Opposition's anti-SIR-CEC march turns into INDIA bloc-government face-off
text: The eight-hour dharna by opposition netas ended with their detentions NEW DELHI: The opposition's protest march to Election Commission headquarters on the SIR-CEC issue Tuesday turned into a high-octane confrontation between Modi govt and INDIA bloc, leading to an eight-hour dharna by Rahul Gandhi and his colleagues at Akashvani Bhavan and ending with their detention in late-evening police action. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress MPs and functionaries forced their way onto the Akashvani premises, after the march by a large contingent of INDIA bloc-BJD MPs was stopped midway by police. The MPs, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Sanjay Raut, Supriya Sule and Abhishek Banerjee, started from Parliament for the EC office amid slogans targeting PM Narendra Modi, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and BJP. But the group was stopped just metres away by heavy police deployment and barricades. Watch Rahul Climbs Barricade, Enters Akashvani Bhawan With Priyanka During EC March Against Gyanesh Kumar The marchers, aided by Congress and SP workers, sat on a dharna on the road outside Akashvani Bhavan. Congress sources claimed govt approached through police and offered permission for five-seven members to meet the CEC, but the party brass insisted on a larger contingent comprising all alliance partners. title: 'Gyanesh Kumar hatao, EC bachao': Congress puts up posters targeting CEC in Delhi
text: NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday upped the ante against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and put up posters demanding his removal in Delhi amid the ongoing row over the functioning of the poll panel and Special Intensive Revision of electoral list. Put up by the Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee's OBC department, the poster read, "Remove Gyanesh Kumar, save Election Commission." This came a day after Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at Gyanesh Kumar after reports of differences within the poll body over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls sparked a political stir. Rahul accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation". "The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference. "I come from a political family, and I have spent more than 50 years in a political family... In India, there is a fundamental force called anti-incumbency that very quickly starts to resist any government. It does not spare anybody. Indira Gandhi won the Bangladesh war, was at the height of her popularity, and then suddenly, within a year or two, massive anti-incumbency, massive pressure," he added. Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed outside the Election Commission office in Delhi ahead of a protest demonstration by Delhi Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. The Indian Youth Congress is also scheduled to hold a protest march from 5, Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar on Friday, demanding the resignation of Kumar. The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Thursday also launched a nationwide online citizens' petition titled "Gyanesh, It's Done Bro", seeking action against the CEC and calling upon citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability. title: FIR on CJP for unlawful assembly, traffic disruption at Shivaji Park stir in Mumbai
text: An FIR has been lodged against the Cockroach Janta Party after their protest at Shivaji Park MUMBAI: Police registered an FIR against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) for allegedly holding an unlawful assembly, raising slogans, disrupting the smooth flow of traffic and using loudspeakers without permission during a protest at Shivaji Park on Friday. CJP supporters were protesting, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over concerns surrounding Election Commission and SIR. According to the FIR, around 400 to 500 unidentified supporters and protesters, including CJP members Ajinkya Shinde, Pranay Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Afreen Nawaz, Soumya Korde, Ankit Bhardwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingale, gathered at the protest venue at 2 pm and stayed put until 7 pm. According to the FIR, the protesters gathered on a public road, allegedly obstructed traffic and raised slogans, leading to a law-and-order situation. Police also alleged that loudspeakers were used to address the gathering without the required permission. The FIR has been registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including those relating to unlawful assembly and disobedience of a lawful order, along with provisions of the Maharashtra Police Act. CJP organised a âJail Bharoâ protest on Friday, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, amid reports of differences within Election Commission. Despite heavy police deployment and denial of formal permission for the protest at Shivaji Park, a large number of citizens and supporters gathered at the venue. Meanwhile, Shivaji Park resident and advocate Siddhi Deolekar too filed a police complaint against Abhijeet Dipke and others, alleging illegal gathering and protest. Deolekar said she lodged the complaint against Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ratna Singh, alleging that they proceeded with the protest and attempted to gather a large crowd despite not having any required permissions. The joint opposition made it clear that their protest will continue undeterred and a bigger protest plan is in the works for Thursday. However, Delhi Police said restrictions imposed under BNSSâs Section 163 were in force in the New Delhi area, which is why the protesters were detained. âAs Section 163 is in force hereâ¦ protest marches or demonstrations are not allowed without permission,â DCP Sachin Sharma said. It all began with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge hosting INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at a restaurant in Janpath, which began around 1.30pm and where the gathering was informed about a plan to continue the protest against CEC, this time with a march to Jantar Mantar for a demonstration. Members, including Congressâs Rahul, KC Venugopal and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, John Brittas (CPM), P Sandosh Kumar (CPI), Manoj Jha (RJD), Derek OâBrien (TMC), Thol Thirumavalavan (VCK), emerged from the restaurant and announced the protest plan. MPs of JMM and IUML also joined them. They headed for buses waiting for them to leave. But the administration had stationed police in heavy numbers at Janpath, which, coupled with the gathering of onlookers and rush of political workers, made it difficult for the buses to move. Some Congress MPs and functionaries climbed on the roof of one of the buses, waving Tricolour. The MPs were forced to dismount from the buses in front of the hotel, where they were surrounded by police. Priyanka, Raja Warring and Deepender Hooda sat down on the road along with some workers, even as the cops continued to request Rahul to get into a bus. Cops finally picked up Rahul and took him away in a mini van. Similarly, Priyanka, who was lying on the street clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women workers of her party, was removed. Police claimed that some protesters attacked their personnel. A sub-inspector alleged protesters bit him and tore his uniform. Police are also analysing mobile-phone videos following allegations that police personnel, including women, were assaulted near Jantar Mantar. Kharge and Rahul said the opposition will continue with its protests till CEC resigns. On an FIR being registered against him for entering Akashvani Bhavan premises and staging an eight-hour sit-in Tuesday, Rahul said, âI have 45 FIRs against me. My target is that there should be 100 FIRs against me. Every FIR against me is a medal for me.â Rahul said the opposition decided to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar, which is the designated protest site, as govt told them that dharna couldnât be held at places like Election Commission. title: 'Not talking on behalf of EC': Union minister says 'no proof' of EC-SIR row, slams opposition
text: Election officials during a meeting amid the ongoing SIR controversy NEW DELHI: Union minister Prahlad Joshi on Saturday hit out at the opposition over its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid the ongoing controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying there was no âconcrete proofâ to support the allegations being raised against the Election Commission. Reacting to the opposition's claims, Joshi said the protest was an expression of the âpainâ caused by its electoral defeat. He said the SIR issue was being used to voice that distress. Watch When The Umpires Clash: 10 Questions At The Heart Of The Election Commission-SIR Row âThe pain in their hearts caused by their defeat... they are trying to express that distress through the SIR issue,â Joshi said. His remarks came in response to questions about a report published by The Indian Express, which cited concerns allegedly raised within the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period. The reports led the opposition to seek action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demand a halt to the SIR, while the ECI said internal notes, queries and differences of view are part of its functioning and maintained that all final decisions on the exercise were unanimous. Joshi said that even if the report was taken into consideration, it did not amount to conclusive evidence of wrongdoing. âWhatever has appeared in The Indian Express... if you even believe that, I am not saying they have no right, but I am also saying that it is not concrete proof for that. It is not at all concrete proof,â he said. Joshi also disputed the opposition's suggestion that decisions related to the SIR were taken unilaterally. Referring to the Election Commission's own press release, he said decisions of the poll panel had been unanimous. âAnd whatever has been written in The Indian Express, even that never states that a unilateral decision was taken. All the decisionsâall, I am not saying almostâall the decisions of the Election Commission have been taken unanimously,â Joshi said. title: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, BJP
text: Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, along with party workers during a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Chandigarh on Friday Chandigarh: Congress workers staged a protest in Chandigarh on Friday, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, whom they accused of âsubverting and sabotagingâ the electoral process. The protesters marched towards the Election Commission office in Sector 17, but the police stopped them midway. Police used water cannons and barricades to prevent the Congress workers from proceeding further. The protesters were detained and later released. Watch âPadma Bhushan Is Small, Make Him PMâ: Pawan Khera Mocks BJPâs Praise For Gyanesh Kumar During the protest, Congress workers raised slogans against Kumar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah , alleging that they were acting in collusion to undermine the electoral process and âsteal electionsâ. Addressing the demonstration, Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said that day by day more evidence was cropping up on how âcompromisedâ the CEC was and how much he was colluding with the BJP to help it steal the elections. He said this had never happened in the history of the country. âWhat is seen to be an electoral victory is actually the theft of the elections (vote-chori),â he said, adding that this happened in Haryana and Maharashtra. He said nobody believed that the BJP could win in these two states when it had badly lost there in the parliamentary elections just a few months before. He alleged that the 2024 parliamentary elections were also rigged. Warring reiterated that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab must be scrapped as it was an instrument only to disfranchise the genuine voters whom the BJP suspected would not vote for it. He said the ensuing assembly elections in Punjab must be held based on the previous electoral rolls used during the parliamentary elections. The Ludhiana MP also accused CEC Kumar of denying first-time voters the right to vote by making registration of fresh voters virtually impossible. He said the strict conditions in Form-6 for first-time voters were humanly impossible to fulfil. This is just an attempt to deny the younger generation, Gen Z, their franchise because the BJP is convinced they will never vote for the party, Warring added. Former deputy chief minister Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said Rahul Gandhi had been saying it for the last three years that the Election Commission of India was working in collusion with the BJP and they were together rigging the elections. Randhawa said both the BJP and the ECI had been exposed in front of the people of this country. He said they had caused immense damage to the credibility of elections in the country and it would take a long time to redeem it. The Gurdaspur MP said the first step to repair the damaged and broken electoral system in the country was to âremove the current CECâ. Former chief minister and Jalandhar MP Charanjit Singh Channi and leader of the opposition in the Punjab assembly, Partap Singh Bajwa, were conspicuous by their absence from the protest. However, Warring defended their absence, saying the protest was planned at short notice and the two leaders might have had prior commitments. Had they not been occupied with other commitments, they would have definitely participated, said Warring. âWhatever issues we had have all been resolved. We are all together. We have set aside personal interests and are fighting collectively against the AAP govt,â Warring added. Several other senior Congress functionaries, including Suraj Thakur, secretary, AICC; Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi; PPCC working president Sukhwinder Singh Danny; working president Raj Kumar Verka; Vijay Inder Singla, co treasurer, AICC; Amit Vij, treasurer, PPCC; Sandeep Singh Sandhu, general secretary, PPCC; MLAs Tript Rajinder Singh Bajwa, Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, Rana Gurjeet Singh, Pargat Singh, and Kuldeep Singh Kala Dhilloon; Rana Kanwarpal Singh, former speaker of the Punjab assembly; former MP Jasbir Singh Dimpa; former Punjab Youth Congress president Amarpreet Lally; and Mohit Mohindra, were also participated in the protest. title: Congress calls bandh on Oct 8 over CEC, textbook, MMDR row
text: Congress and other INDIA bloc constituents hold a protest rally in Bhubaneswar on Tuesday Bhubaneswar: Congress on Tuesday called for a statewide bandh on Oct 8, demanding resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar amid nationwide political controversy over large-scale deletions of voters during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The opposition party also cited the demands for rollback of the amended MMDR Act, 2026, and resignation of state school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond over alleged large-scale errors in school textbooks as key reasons for the ensuing shutdown. The bandh call comes close on heels of a similar statewide shutdown announced by Navnirman Krushak Sangathan, a farmersâ outfit, for Wednesday over textbook errors. âOur Odisha bandh on Oct 8 is primarily aimed at seeking resignations of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over voter-list manipulations and school minister Nityananda Gond over large-scale textbook errors, besides demanding withdrawal of the amended mining law. We have sought the support of all INDIA bloc partners for the bandh,â Congress Odisha president Bhakta Charan Das said on the sidelines of a protest rally organised by INDIA bloc constituents near the assembly here on Tuesday protesting alleged voter-list deletions, MMDR Act and textbook blunders. Referring to Congress MP Rahul Gandhiâs allegations regarding the SIR exercise and electoral rolls, Das said concerns over the functioning and impartiality of Election Commission of India could not be sidelined. The protest rally, held a day after the BJDâs agitation against the MMDR Act amendments, also targeted the BJP govt for allegedly getting the assemblyâs monsoon session adjourned sine die on Monday, five days before its scheduled conclusion on Oct 3. âThe BJP lacked the courage to face our members in the House on issues relating to the MMDR Act amendments and textbook errors. Our agitation will continue. On Oct 7, we will organise a massive âParivartan Rallyâ in Keonjhar district,â Das said. BJP MLA Tankadhar Tripathy dismissed the oppositionâs allegations, accusing it of spreading misinformation. âThere was no manipulation of electoral rolls. The amendments to the MMDR Act will benefit the state and streamline mining activities and mineral taxation. The govt has already initiated action against those responsible for the textbook errors, and the crime branch probe is underway,â Tripathy said.
